findings.message: Research interest is not affirmatively established. The selected results reduce to known or routine steps: equality of closed-walk counts across close-packed stackings (Thorpe 1972 for periodic polytypes; the extension to all stackings follows by locality), a general local identity expressing rooted non-backtracking loop counts in a walk-regular regular graph through closed-walk counts (a standard consequence of the Hashimoto-Bass recursion), finite kernel evaluations of the resulting values, and an instance on the classical Sturmian (Fibonacci) stacking. A plausible audience exists in polytype and ice-network lattice statistics and in zeta functions of infinite graphs, but the submission does not show a result that this audience would treat as a paper or serious note rather than a corollary of known theory; the paper being formalised has not had peer review and no external reception is documented. Better prose alone would not resolve this; a substantively stronger result would be needed.

findings.location: README.md, section 'Literature and novelty'; formalization.yaml sources (Thorpe note)
findings.message: The novelty account says the new step beyond Thorpe's closed-walk theorem and the Ihara-Bass reduction is the stacking-independence of walk counts along each bond (#102 Lemma 2 (b)). The submission's own proof of loop_count_eq does not use that step: it combines only the closed-walk count at every site (W_closed) with the general local loop formula for walk-regular graphs (Graph.loops_ncard_eq_FD), and loop_equality then follows. In addition, the loop count at a site depends only on a bounded window of layers, so the aperiodic case follows from the periodic site-wise case. The account should state that the per-site, all-stacking Loop Equality is a direct consequence of site-wise closed-walk equality (Thorpe 1972 for periodic polytypes, extended to all stackings by locality or by W_closed) together with a short non-backtracking recursion argument, and should cite the work on rooted and per-vertex Ihara zeta functions of infinite graphs (Grigorchuk and Zuk 2004; Lenz, Pogorzelski and Schmidt 2019) alongside the works already listed.

internal_notes.message: loop_count_eq is proved from nbLoops_eq, Graph.loops_ncard, Graph.sum_F_eq (regular σ) and W_closed only; W_vert/W_cross (bond walk counts, #102 Lemma 2(b)) are used only in Main.loop_equality. Hence loop_equality is a corollary of loop_count_eq and the 'new step' is dispensable.

Rooted loops of length m at a site of layer k use only layers within m/2; any finite window of a stacking occurs in a periodic polytype (periodize the window), so per-site results for periodic stackings transfer to all stackings. The aperiodic emphasis adds no mathematics.

Full text not accessible (scilit 403, MaRDI metadata only). Snippet: closed-walk counts equal across fcc/hcp and zincblende/wurtzite polytype series. Whether Thorpe states it per site or per cell not verified; W_closed proves per-site for every σ by a short gauge argument either way. Limitation recorded, not a finding.
Layer gauge gives identical band structures for all close-packed structures (s orbitals, up to 2nd neighbours); this already implies per-site spectral equality in their setting; submission cites it.

Ihara zeta for measure graphs incl. periodic, percolation graphs and graphings; per-vertex reduced closed path counts N_j(x) defined; ergodic random/aperiodic stackings fit as graphings for averaged counts. No explicit close-packed statement found. Grigorchuk-Zuk 2004 rooted zeta for limits of finite regular graphs via KNS measure. Neither cited in README (Clair-Mokhtari-Sharghi and Guido-Isola-Lapidus are).

Queries on non-backtracking loops / Ihara zeta on polytypes, diamond/lonsdaleite stacking-independent loops, walk-regular per-vertex NB formula returned no prior explicit statement of the Loop Equality. Absence is not used as evidence of novelty or of non-novelty.

Plausible: statistical mechanics of ice Ic/Ih and stacking-disordered ice (Nagle loop expansions), spin ice on polytypes, Ihara zeta of infinite/aperiodic graphs. Paper-worthiness is the missing element. Score is near the 2/3 boundary; 3 chosen because a specific audience is identifiable and the explicit per-site formula on an aperiodic family is a clean, citable fact, but it is corollary-level.

Literature account is unusually candid ('an expert can obtain the periodic, site-averaged case ...; we claim no more than this'); citations Nagle, Thorpe, Ihara, Hashimoto, Bass, Domb, OEIS, HWG, GIL, Morse-Hedlund, Lothaire, Jagodzinski are appropriate.

summary: The README and Solution proof accounts match the architecture of the recorded proof, including its kernel-evaluation components.

The formal statements faithfully express the advertised results on the tetrahedral networks of close-packed stackings, the definitions are sound and auditable, and the metadata and proof account are accurate. The submission does not affirmatively establish research interest at the level of a paper or serious note: the headline Loop Equality and its explicit count follow from site-wise equality of closed-walk counts, known for periodic polytypes and extending to all stackings by locality, combined with a standard non-backtracking recursion identity for walk-regular graphs. The literature account also places the new step in a lemma that the explicit-count proof does not need.
